sourceEvidence.claim: The Cellular adaptations intro — reversible changes, physiologic (uterine enlargement during pregnancy) vs pathologic (myocardial hypertrophy 2° to systemic hypertension), and the progression to cell injury (significant LV hypertrophy → myocardial injury → HF)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Cellular adaptations

Reversible changes that can be physiologic (eg, uterine enlargement during pregnancy) or pathologic
(eg, myocardial hypertrophy 2° to systemic hypertension). If stress is excessive or persistent,
adaptations can progress to cell injury (eg, significant LV hypertrophy → myocardial injury → HF).

sourceEvidence.claim: Hyperplasia — controlled proliferation of stem cells and differentiated cells → ↑ in number of cells (benign prostatic hyperplasia); excessive stimulation → pathologic hyperplasia (endometrial) which may progress to dysplasia and cancer
sourceEvidence.quote:
Hyperplasia

Controlled proliferation of stem cells and differentiated cells → ↑ in number of cells (eg, benign
prostatic hyperplasia). Excessive stimulation → pathologic hyperplasia (eg, endometrial
hyperplasia), which may progress to dysplasia and cancer.

sourceEvidence.claim: Atrophy — ↓ in tissue mass via ↓ size (ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, autophagy, ↓ protein synthesis) and/or ↓ number (apoptosis); the five causes
sourceEvidence.quote:

↓ in tissue mass due to ↓ in size (↑ cytoskeleton degradation via ubiquitin-proteasome pathway

sourceEvidence.claim: Metaplasia — stem-cell reprogramming, Barrett esophagus (acid → intestinal-type columnar), the airway opposite (tobacco smoke → stratified squamous), progression risk (Barrett → esophageal adenocarcinoma), and connective-tissue metaplasia (myositis ossificans)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Metaplasia

Reprogramming of stem cells → replacement of one cell type by another that can adapt to a new
stressor. Esophageal exposure to gastric acid: nonkeratinized stratified squamous → intestinal-type
columnar epithelium (acid resistance), called Barrett esophagus. The opposite occurs upon airway
exposure to tobacco smoke: pseudostratified ciliated columnar → stratified squamous epithelium
(protection). May progress to dysplasia → malignant transformation with persistent insult (eg,
Barrett esophagus → esophageal adenocarcinoma). Metaplasia of connective tissue can also occur
(eg, myositis ossificans, the formation of bone within muscle after trauma).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Dysplasia — disordered precancerous epithelial growth, not a true adaptive response; pleomorphism, loss of orientation, nuclear changes; the mild/moderate vs severe fork; usually preceded by persistent metaplasia or pathologic hyperplasia
sourceEvidence.quote:
Dysplasia

Disordered, precancerous epithelial cell growth; not considered a true adaptive response.
Characterized by loss of uniformity of cell size and shape (pleomorphism); loss of tissue
orientation; nuclear changes (eg, ↑ nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio and clumped chromatin). Mild and
moderate dysplasias (ie, do not involve entire thickness of epithelium) may regress with alleviation
of inciting cause. Severe dysplasia often becomes irreversible and progresses to carcinoma in situ.
Usually preceded by persistent metaplasia or pathologic hyperplasia.
